doc.title: Pierre Boussaguet interviewed by Matthieu Jaffre, Aix en Provence, France, July 28, 2020

title: Hot Club teacher and the Coleman Hawkins record bought in Toulouse
summary: His first trip to Toulouse, buying Coleman Hawkins and Howard McGhee records, and his teacher's disapproval.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Yeah. I mean the new world. And of course the first thing I did in Toulouse is to buy a couple of records.
And I bought that great Coleman Hawkins/Howard McGhee record with Tommy Potter.
So during the late 40s I guess, middle.
Yeah. Beginning of the 50s. Art Blakey of course. And —
Some of the youngsters, beboppers from that time.
Yeah. So at that time you select a record, you go to the guy of the shop and you ask him, I don’t know about it — he’d play a few notes, you say okay, I want it.
I like it. I want to buy it.

Or, I don’t know, and you’d try something else. So I went back home with that Coleman Hawkins and I was so proud because the guy has teach me about Coleman Hawkins. “Body and Soul,” like in ‘37, all of that. And when I got home with the new record that I bought, I’m very proud. Like I am nourishing a new regime with a teacher. And when I got, the next week, he said, “Oh you bought some records. What is that?” He said, “Oh bad luck?” You bought a record where, that’s an area where Coleman Hawkins started to play not only jazz. And somewhere, I tell this whole story because it can happen today, which any form of music or art. Like someone is dogmatic. I can’t stand that. You listen to something, it speaks to you or not, but you can’t judge a music, like who can judge if one music is better than the other one.
